title: Post-Consultation Pulmonary Procedure & Follow-up Plan Explanation

chapters.title: Patient Interview & Symptom Review
chapters.summary: Patient discusses persistent mild cough and activity-related shortness of breath over 3 weeks.

chapters.title: Doctor Discussion of Chest CT Findings
chapters.summary: Physician reviews the CT chest scan showing a 6mm right upper lobe subpleural nodule and explains Fleischner Society follow-up protocol.

chapters.title: Procedure Explanation & Next Steps
chapters.summary: Discussion of pulmonary function test (PFT) and scheduled follow-up CT scan in 6 months.

transcription.speaker: Dr. Jenkins
transcription.text: Hello, today we are reviewing the results of your chest CT scan performed yesterday.

transcription.speaker: Patient
transcription.text: I've been feeling a bit short of breath when taking long walks, and the cough hasn't gone away.

transcription.speaker: Dr. Jenkins
transcription.text: The CT scan showed a tiny 6 millimeter nodule in the upper portion of your right lung. This is very small and very common.

transcription.speaker: Dr. Jenkins
transcription.text: Standard clinical guidelines recommend repeating a low-dose CT in 6 to 12 months to make sure it remains stable.

transcription.speaker: Dr. Jenkins
transcription.text: We will also schedule a routine blood panel and pulmonary function test next month.

visible_observations: Physician demonstrating 3D chest anatomy model on screen; patient in consultation room.
questions_for_physician: Should I monitor for any specific symptoms like fever or severe chest pain before the 6-month scan?
Do I need to make any lifestyle adjustments or dietary changes before the upcoming PFT test?
